search_log: Searched “Ask Again, Yes” Mary Beth Keane excerpt publisher; found and opened the official Simon & Schuster excerpt and Penguin Books sample.
Searched “Ask Again, Yes” “third person” and “third person omniscient”; opened the explicit BookRags whole-book POV description.

Searched “Ask Again, Yes” point of view, narrator, and multiple perspectives; results from reviews and study guides consistently described shifting character perspectives, with no evidence of sustained first- or second-person sections.
Opened the Georgia Public Broadcasting author interview to verify the whole-book multi-character viewpoint structure.
Searched the exact phrase “Then and now, I say yes”; surrounding context identifies it as Kate’s spoken reply to Peter, so it is local dialogue rather than a first-person narrative strand.
person_note: The authorized opening sample sustains nonparticipating third-person narration while shifting close focalization from Francis to Lena, and the many interior Goodreads passages continue that pattern across Peter, Kate, Anne, Brian, and others. Whole-book web descriptions likewise identify third-person omniscient narration with changing character proximity. The novel’s multiple perspectives are shifts in focalization, not sustained changes of grammatical person. Generic “you” and “we” passages do not indicate second or first person, and q04237’s isolated “I” is confirmed as Kate’s dialogue. No credible contrary narrative-person evidence remains.
